about.title: Visalia Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Visalia sits at the center of Tulare County, and the products people rely on here range from farm equipment and irrigation parts to the airbags and tires in vehicles that travel SR-198 and S Mooney Boulevard every day. When one of those products fails and someone gets hurt, California law offers a path that does not depend on proving carelessness. Under strict liability, an injured person generally needs to show that the product was defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused the injury. That distinction matters. A manufacturer can have followed every internal procedure and still be responsible for a design that was unsafe. Distributors and retailers can share that responsibility too. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Visalia residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles defective-product claims, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. If a product hurt you, keep it, and let us help you find someone to review what happened.

whyChoose.title: Why Visalia Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You don't have to prove the maker was careless
items.desc: California product claims generally run on strict liability, so the question is whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not whether anyone intended harm. An attorney in our network can explain how that standard applies to your situation.

items.title: More than one company may owe you
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Visalia retailer who sold the product can all be held responsible under California law. Identifying every party in that chain is something an experienced attorney does early.

items.title: We help you protect the evidence that matters most
items.desc: The product itself is often the heart of a defect case, and throwing it away or returning it can weaken your claim. We connect you quickly with an attorney who can guide you on preserving it.

items.question: My tire blew out on SR-198 near Visalia. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both, and the answer depends on what caused the blowout. If the tire had a manufacturing flaw or a design problem, a product liability claim against the tire maker or seller may exist alongside any claim from the collision itself. Keep the tire and the wheel, and avoid letting a shop discard them before an attorney has reviewed the situation.

items.question: What counts as a "defect" under California law?
items.answer: California recognizes three types: a design defect, where the whole product line is unsafe as planned; a manufacturing defect, where a particular unit came out wrong; and a warning defect, where the product lacked adequate instructions or hazard warnings. You generally need to show one of these existed and that it caused your injury. Proving the company was negligent is usually not required.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Visalia, not from the manufacturer. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Yes. Under California's strict liability rules, retailers and distributors can be responsible for a defective product they placed into the stream of commerce, even if they never opened the box. This matters when a manufacturer is overseas or hard to reach. An attorney can help sort out which parties belong in the claim.
